headline: High: Copilot can write repo files while kotaemon ingests broad documents and API keys, creating default-path leakage and action-conflict risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Copilot reads repo context and open editor buffers, while kotaemon uses a web UI over documents and chat transcripts. No shared channel is documented, so direct injection is not proven; the plausible bridge is manual copy/paste or file handoff, which is lower risk than default shared-state pathways.
conditions: IF an operator copies kotaemon-generated text into Copilot chat or files, prompt injection becomes possible.
IF both agents are pointed at the same manually shared document, attacker-controlled instructions can traverse the bridge.
mitigations: Disable copy/paste of untrusted model output into Copilot prompts.
Keep kotaemon outputs in a separate review buffer before reuse.
Use a human-only approval step for any instruction-like text.
requires-engineering: add provenance labels to shared artifacts.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Copilot reads repo context and open editor buffers, and kotaemon touches documents, PDFs, chat transcripts, and API keys while calling third-party LLM APIs. A shared workspace or copied file can expose sensitive content from one agent to the other, and kotaemon's broad egress makes leakage more consequential than local-only tools.
conditions: IF kotaemon is given files from the same repository or workspace as Copilot, sensitive code or secrets can flow into external APIs.
IF Copilot edits files that kotaemon later ingests, those contents can be transmitted to third-party inference backends.
mitigations: Separate kotaemon and Copilot workspaces.
Remove secrets from any shared folder before ingestion.
Restrict kotaemon to local-only models for sensitive projects.
Rotate any API keys that were present in shared documents.
requires-engineering: enforce per-tool data-loss-prevention filters.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Copilot can write the filesystem and modify git state, while kotaemon uses a web UI and stores data under ./ktem_app_data. If both operate on the same repository or mounted volume, they can overwrite each other's changes or create conflicting git/workspace state; no locking is documented.
conditions: IF kotaemon and Copilot share the same writable directory, concurrent edits can clobber files.
IF kotaemon writes artifacts into a repo that Copilot is also modifying, git state conflicts can occur.
mitigations: Use separate working directories.
Pause one agent before the other writes.
Commit or snapshot before switching tools.
Avoid mounting ./ktem_app_data inside the repo.
requires-engineering: add file locks around shared mutable paths.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Copilot produces code edits and chat output that a human may pass into kotaemon, and kotaemon can summarize or act on documents and citations. Because kotaemon's web UI and API-backed workflow can treat upstream text as input without a documented verification gate, errors from Copilot can cascade into downstream answers or actions.
conditions: IF Copilot-generated code or prose is imported into kotaemon as source material, downstream summaries may inherit errors.
IF an operator relies on kotaemon outputs without checking the original Copilot context, mistaken facts can propagate.
mitigations: Verify Copilot output against source files before ingestion.
Require citations back to original documents.
Use a second reviewer for any action based on kotaemon output.
Keep generated text separate from authoritative sources.
requires-engineering: add provenance checks between tools.

E_compliance.rationale: Copilot is tied to GitHub repo context and vendor APIs, while kotaemon handles documents, chat transcripts, and API keys through third-party model providers. The pair can therefore move regulated or sensitive content into different retention and residency regimes; no shared compliance controls are documented, so the safer choice is medium rather than low.
conditions: IF EU personal data or confidential documents are placed into kotaemon, they may be processed by external model providers under different retention rules.
IF repository content subject to GitHub policies is copied into kotaemon, compliance obligations may diverge.
mitigations: Classify data before sending it to either tool.
Keep regulated data out of kotaemon unless approved.
Review vendor retention settings for each backend.
Use separate tenants for sensitive and non-sensitive work.
requires-engineering: document a data-processing agreement and residency map.
